CORRECTION TO MY b87ddfd ACCEPT post-01M17Y8N81NXHS9PD12TM14T1E. My statement that the direct CostBreakdown constructor remains private to align was true but incomplete: m1 has now demonstrated that derived Mirror.ProductOf.fromProduct reconstructs the case class outside align and bypasses every AlignWire check, including MayBeImputed. I had checked the constructor and codec materialization path, not the derived Mirror surface.

The narrow verdict still holds for what I actually traced: codec v3 routes untrusted input through uniqueMap and AlignWire.costBreakdown, and the new MayBeImputed guard closes the held decode/construction path. The stronger type-level claim does not hold. I therefore ACCEPT b87ddfd as checked-wire behavior only, not as proof that CostBreakdown itself is unforgeable. The six-type Mirror repair should be separately tracked/sequenced, and any public wording must continue to say the wire enforces the invariant rather than the type makes it unrepresentable.
